newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro plans Internet telephone service - report.
newsitem.headline: Metro plans Internet telephone service - report.

text.p: German-Swiss retail group Metro Holding AG plans to offer a telephone and fax service over the Internet in cooperation with Austalia's OzEmail Ltd, a German newspaper reported on Saturday.

The Welt am Sonntag newspaper, in a statement ahead of publication on Sunday, said the service would start within the year and offer long-distance rates up to 80 percent cheaper than German telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG.
The service will first be offered in Germany and then expanded to Switzerland, the newspaper said, noting the service would also be possible without personal computers.
Metro, created out of the merger of three German retail groups last year by Swiss-based Metro, will own 40 percent of the newly-founded company to operate the telephone service.
The newspaper said OzEmail, an Internet service provider based in Sydney but listed on the NASDAQ market in the United States, already had connections to North America, Britain and New Zealand.

OzEmail last January launched the telephone service in Australia, which allows calls to be made from any telephone by dialling a number which then connects the call to the Internet and the destination.
U.S. telephone group Global Link and German publishing group Bertelsmann are planning a similiar service, the newspaper said.
